title: The $\varepsilon$-$t$-Net Problem
statement_text: How small are the smallest $\varepsilon$-$t$-nets for $H$? Can we compute them efficiently?
context_text: Given a finite hypergraph $H=(V,E)$, a positive integer $t$, and $\varepsilon\in(t/|V|,1)$, an $\varepsilon$-$t$-net for $H$ is a family $S\subseteq\binom{V}{t}$ of $t$-element subsets of $V$ such that every hyperedge $e\in E$ with $|e|\geq\varepsilon|V|$ contains some $s\in S$ as a subset. For $t=1$ this is the classical notion of an $\varepsilon$-net (a set of vertices hitting every hyperedge of size at least $\varepsilon|V|$), and for $t=\Theta(\varepsilon|V|)$ it corresponds to $\varepsilon$-Mnets; the minimum size of an $\varepsilon$-$t$-net is sandwiched between the minimum sizes of $\varepsilon$-nets and of Mnets. The question is posed for general hypergraphs, with motivations from secret sharing (distributing keys to $t$-subsets so that any sufficiently large coalition of a prescribed kind can open a lock), Turán numbers of hypergraphs (a smallest $(k/n)$-$t$-net of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices has size $\binom{n}{t}-T(n,k,t)$), $\chi$-boundedness and edge-colouring of hypergraphs. The authors prove that every hypergraph of VC-dimension $d$ (and dual shatter function $\pi^*_H(m)\le Cm^{d^*}$) on at least $C_1((t-1)/\varepsilon)^{d^*}$ vertices has an $\varepsilon$-$t$-net of size $O(\frac{d(1+\log t)}{\varepsilon}\log\frac1\varepsilon)$, which is tight for $t=O(1)$; that hypergraphs of VC-dimension 1 have $\varepsilon$-$t$-nets of size at most $t\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil+1$; give an explicit (efficient) construction of size $O_d(\varepsilon^{-(d+t-1)})$ for hypergraphs of $t$-VC-dimension $d$; and obtain $O(1/\varepsilon)$-size $\varepsilon$-2-nets for several geometric hypergraphs in the plane.
